dedupe_keys.name: diva coastal impact and adaptation modelling divacoast jl and global diva datasets

description: DIVA (originally Dynamic Interactive Vulnerability Assessment) is an ecosystem of tools and data for modelling the biophysical and socio-economic impacts of sea level rise and the effect of adaptation such as dike raising and beach nourishment, covering coastal flooding, erosion, wetland change and salinity intrusion. The first version came from the EU project DINAS-COAST; the current DIVACoast.jl is a Julia library with data types and algorithms for scripting assessment runs, with demo data and scripts, and a global dataset on Zenodo partitions the world's coastal plain into about 175,000 flood plains and the coastline into about 700,000 segments, as GeoTIFF and GeoPackage files with NUTS2 and GADM1 tables (about 4.3 GB, April 2026, CC BY 4.0). Global Climate Forum coordinates development and maintains the code, with bio-physical modules from the University of Southampton, coastal input data from Kiel University and wetland modules from Cambridge and Lincoln. The library is open source under the MIT licence on GitHub with online documentation. Caveats: the library version is still 0.0.0, the dataset's method paper was in preparation, and users must script their own runs. It supports national to global coastal flood exposure, damage and adaptation cost scenarios for infrastructure; a related record is the Coastal Hazard Wheel.
